newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Wal-Mart leads spread parade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Wal-Mart leads spread parade.

text.p: Individual equity options volume was heavy on Monday, but much of it was from a few sizable spreads, traders said.
The biggest was in Wal-Mart Stores Inc options on the Chicago Board Options Exchange, where a June/January call spread crossed about 18,400 times.
The WalMart January 22-1/2 call traded 18,395 contracts and the June 22-1/2 call traded 18,380.
"It was just a spread to a large customer," a trader said. "They bought the Junes and sold out the Januarys."
Walmart shares were up 3/8 at 31-3/4 Monday afternoon.
The WalMart June 22-1/2 call had open interest of about 17,430 contracts and the January 22-1/2 call had open interest of 5,675.
Few other WalMart options were busy.
In other trading, a large spread crossed in calls on shares of Boston Scientific Corp, which were down one at 56-1/4.
The August 60 call traded 9,235 contracts and the August 55 call traded 9,155. The spread was done 9,150 times.
Open interest in the August 60 calls was 800 and 9,725 in the August 55s.
Also, most of the volume in PairGain Technologies Inc July 17-1/2 and January 15 puts crossed as spreads.
The July 17-1/2 put traded about 1,870 contracts and the January 15 put traded 1,850. Open interest was 624 and 57, respectively.
The stock was up 3/16 at 17-3/4.
Elsewhere, options on shares of Office Depot Inc remained active at the American Stock Exchange as the stock waffled around unchanged levels.
Office Depot was up 1/8 at 17-1/2 in afternoon activity on turnover of about 1.15 million shares.
Office Depot July options were again the highlight, led by the July 20 call, which traded nearly 8,400 contracts. Open interest was 44,734 contracts.
Also on the call side, the July 15s traded about 7,970 contracts and the July 22-1/2s traded 2,765.
The July 12-1/2 put traded nearly 5,000 contracts and the July 15 put traded 4,780.

Traders said investors are using the July series instead of June because they do not expect a U.S. District Court judge's decision on Office Depot's planned merger with Staples Inc by the June 21 expiration of June options.
